hints: Focus on what each axis means, electronegativity measures pull on bonding electrons while first ionisation energy measures removal of an outer electron.
Recall the smooth trend in electronegativity across Period 3, from Na lowest to Si highest, so check the vertical order first.
Now remember the dip in first ionisation energy from Mg to Al, so Al must sit to the left of Mg on the horizontal axis even though it is higher up.
walkthrough:
**Order the electronegativity values**

Think across Period 3 from Na to Si. Nuclear charge increases and atomic radius decreases, so pull on electrons increases smoothly.

Order for y-axis (low to high): $$\text{Na} < \text{Mg} < \text{Al} < \text{Si}$$

**Order the first ionisation energies**

Ionisation energy generally increases across the period, but there is a famous dip from Mg to Al. Mg has a stable full $3s^2$ subshell, while Al loses an easier $3p^1$ electron.

Order for x-axis (low to high): $$\text{Na} < \text{Al} < \text{Mg} < \text{Si}$$

**Combine both orders to find the plot**

Na must be bottom-left (lowest in both). Si must be top-right (highest in both). The key test is Al and Mg. Al is higher than Mg vertically, but to the left of Mg horizontally.

Only one diagram shows Al up and left relative to Mg, with Na at the bottom left and Si at the top right.

options.A: Shows a perfect straight line correlation with order Na < Mg < Al < Si on both axes. This ignores the Period 3 dip where first ionisation energy of Al is lower than Mg due to the $3p^1$ vs $3s^2$ configuration.
options.B: Correct on both axes. Vertically, electronegativity rises Na < Mg < Al < Si. Horizontally, first ionisation energy follows Na < Al < Mg < Si, correctly placing Al to the left of Mg but above it.
options.C: Reverses the electronegativity trend, showing Na highest and Si lowest. Electronegativity increases across a period, not decreases, so Na must be lowest and Si highest.
options.D: Also reverses electronegativity, showing Na at the top and Si at the bottom. It also places Al to the left of Mg correctly for ionisation energy, but the vertical order is completely wrong.
